container_info.description: This project aims to develop a comprehensive functional test plan for Wi-Fi 7 (IEEE 802.11be) devices, focusing on non-performance aspects. The plan will cover Multi-Link Operation (MLO) with mandatory Multi-Link Single Radio (MLSR) and optional Multi-Link Multi Radio (MLMR) scenarios, security validation for WPA2 and WPA3 protocols, and basic stability test cases. The outcome will be a structured, reusable test plan suitable for device certification, QA, and interoperability testing.
container_info.reasoning: The project is about producing a structured, reusable test plan and tooling for Wi‑Fi device functional testing (certification/QA/interoperability), which implies server-side document generation, APIs, and automation orchestration rather than a GUI. The container is labeled 'backend' and already includes Python3, Flask, Sphinx, MkDocs, uvicorn, Celery and many server-side tools. Flask is a lightweight Python web/backend framework present in the image and well suited for a headless container, simple APIs, web hooks, and integration with test automation and documentation generators. It matches the PLATFORM DETECTION GUIDELINES for backend frameworks and adheres to the MINIMAL/ LIGHTWEIGHT rules (use built-in dev server during development, minimal dependencies).

install Flask (pip install --no-cache-dir Flask) for the app core

minimal configuration via environment variables (no secrets manager) and a lightweight .env or env vars

steps.name: environment - prepare sanitized venv and persist PATH
steps.description: Create a sanitized, external Python virtualenv (to avoid workspace path special-character issues) at /opt/venvs/coredoc_govhub if no approved VENV_DIR is provided. Ensure python3/pip and python3-venv are available (install apt packages only if missing), upgrade packaging tools in the venv (best-effort), chown to SUDO_USER when appropriate, and persist the venv bin on PATH via /etc/profile.d/coredoc_govhub.sh. This avoids venv launcher shebang parsing problems when the workspace contains shell-special characters.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/wifi-7-functional-test-plan-4457-4631/CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub"
# Default safe venv location (sanitized, no spaces/special chars). Engineer can override by exporting VENV_DIR before running.
VENV_DIR="${VENV_DIR:-/opt/venvs/coredoc_govhub}"
# ensure minimal system packages exist (non-interactive, quiet)
if ! command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "error: python3 missing" >&2; exit 2; fi
if ! python3 -c "import venv" >/dev/null 2>&1 || ! command -v pip3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
  sudo apt-get update -q >/dev/null || true
  sudo apt-get install -yq python3-pip python3-venv >/dev/null
fi
# create sanitized venv directory if missing
sudo mkdir -p "$(dirname "$VENV_DIR")" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
if [ ! -d "$VENV_DIR" ]; then
  sudo mkdir -p "$VENV_DIR" >/dev/null
  sudo chown "${SUDO_USER:-$(id -un)}" "$VENV_DIR" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  python3 -m venv "$VENV_DIR"
  if [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ] && [ -n "${SUDO_USER:-}" ]; then sudo chown -R "${SUDO_USER}:${SUDO_USER}" "$VENV_DIR" || true; fi
fi
# locate venv python and pip
PY=""
for p in "$VENV_DIR/bin/python3" "$VENV_DIR/bin/python"; do [ -x "$p" ] && { PY="$p"; break; } done
PIP=""
for p in "$VENV_DIR/bin/pip" "$VENV_DIR/bin/pip3"; do [ -x "$p" ] && { PIP="$p"; break; } done
if [ -z "${PY:-}" ] || [ -z "${PIP:-}" ]; then echo "error: venv python or pip missing at $VENV_DIR/bin" >&2; exit 3; fi
# upgrade packaging tools (best-effort, log suppressed)
"$PIP" install --no-cache-dir --upgrade pip setuptools wheel >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
# Persist PATH via /etc/profile.d with a double-quoted VENV_PATH literal
PROFILE="/etc/profile.d/coredoc_govhub.sh"
sudo tee "$PROFILE" >/dev/null <<'EOF'
# CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub venv (added if present)
VENV_PATH="/opt/venvs/coredoc_govhub"
if [ -d "$VENV_PATH" ]; then
  case ":$PATH:" in
    *":${VENV_PATH}/bin:"*) :;;
    *) export PATH="${VENV_PATH}/bin:$PATH" ;;
  esac
fi
EOF
sudo chmod 755 "$PROFILE" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
# quick validation: ensure venv python is runnable
"$PY" -c "import sys; print('venv_ok')" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "error: venv python failed to run" >&2; exit 4; }

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/wifi-7-functional-test-plan-4457-4631/CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub"
mkdir -p "$WORKSPACE" && cd "$WORKSPACE"
ARTIFACTS_DIR="$WORKSPACE/artifacts"
mkdir -p "$WORKSPACE/app" "$WORKSPACE/tests" "$ARTIFACTS_DIR" "$WORKSPACE/docs"
# Minimal Flask app
cat > "$WORKSPACE/app/__init__.py" <<'PY'
from flask import Flask, request, jsonify
import os, json, time
app = Flask(__name__)
ARTIFACTS_DIR = os.environ.get('ARTIFACTS_DIR') or os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), '..', 'artifacts'))
os.makedirs(ARTIFACTS_DIR, exist_ok=True)

@app.get('/')
def index():
    return jsonify({'status': 'ok', 'service': 'CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub'})

@app.post('/results')
def post_results():
    data = request.get_json(silent=True) or {}
    fname = os.path.join(ARTIFACTS_DIR, f"result_{int(time.time())}.json")
    with open(fname, 'w') as f:
        json.dump(data, f)
    return jsonify({'stored': fname}), 201
PY

from app import app
import os
if __name__ == '__main__':
    app.run(host='0.0.0.0', port=int(os.environ.get('PORT', '5000')), debug=(os.environ.get('FLASK_DEBUG','0')=='1'))
PY

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/wifi-7-functional-test-plan-4457-4631/CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub"
VENV_DIR="${VENV_DIR:-/opt/venvs/coredoc_govhub}"

PORT=${PORT:-5000}
# Start server
"$PY" "$WORKSPACE/app/wsgi.py" >/tmp/coredoc_server.log 2>&1 &
PID=$!
echo "started $PID" >/tmp/coredoc_server.pid
# Poll health endpoint
MAX_WAIT=30
SECS=0
OK=0
while [ $SECS -lt $MAX_WAIT ]; do
  if curl -sS "http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/" | grep -q '"status":"ok"'; then OK=1; break; fi
  sleep 1; SECS=$((SECS+1))
done
if [ "$OK" -ne 1 ]; then echo "health-check failed; see /tmp/coredoc_server.log" >&2; kill $PID || true; exit 3; fi
# graceful stop
kill $PID || true
wait $PID 2>/dev/null || true
echo "validation: success"

steps.name: dependencies - install Python deps into sanitized venv (with retry and logs)
steps.description: Install runtime dependencies from requirements.txt into the sanitized venv (/opt/venvs/coredoc_govhub by default). Detect if Flask is already importable in the venv and skip reinstall. If TEST=true, install pytest. On pip failures, log output to /tmp and retry once. Use the venv pip executable directly to avoid activation issues.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/wifi-7-functional-test-plan-4457-4631/CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub"
VENV_DIR="${VENV_DIR:-/opt/venvs/coredoc_govhub}"
PY="$VENV_DIR/bin/python3"
[ -x "$PY" ] || PY="$VENV_DIR/bin/python"
PIP="$VENV_DIR/bin/pip"
REQS="$WORKSPACE/requirements.txt"
if [ ! -x "$PY" ] || [ ! -x "$PIP" ]; then echo "error: venv python/pip missing; run env-001" >&2; exit 2; fi
PIP_LOG=/tmp/coredoc_pip_install.log
install_reqs(){ "$PIP" install --no-cache-dir -r "$REQS" >"$PIP_LOG" 2>&1; }
# install only if flask not importable in venv
if ! "$PY" -c "import importlib.util,sys; sys.exit(0 if importlib.util.find_spec('flask') else 1)"; then
  if ! install_reqs; then sleep 1; if ! install_reqs; then echo "error: pip install failed; see $PIP_LOG" >&2; sed -n '1,200p' "$PIP_LOG" >&2 || true; exit 3; fi; fi
fi
# optional pytest

steps.name: validation - start WSGI server (no reloader), health-check (JSON), and clean shutdown
steps.description: Start the WSGI entrypoint directly with the sanitized venv python (avoids Flask CLI reloader), poll the health endpoint until it returns JSON {'status':'ok'} or timeout (MAX_WAIT, default 30s), then terminate the server PID cleanly and report success/failure. Capture server logs to /tmp for diagnosis. This verifies build, start, responsiveness and clean stop for the development environment.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/wifi-7-functional-test-plan-4457-4631/CoreDocumentation&GovernanceHub"
cd "$WORKSPACE"
VENV_DIR="${VENV_DIR:-/opt/venvs/coredoc_govhub}"
PY="$VENV_DIR/bin/python3"
[ -x "$PY" ] || PY="$VENV_DIR/bin/python"
if [ ! -x "$PY" ]; then echo "error: venv python missing; run env-001" >&2; exit 2; fi
export ARTIFACTS_DIR="$WORKSPACE/artifacts"
export FLASK_DEBUG=${FLASK_DEBUG:-0}
export PORT=${PORT:-5000}
LOG=/tmp/coredoc_server.log
MAX_WAIT=${MAX_WAIT:-30}
# start the app directly (no auto-reloader)
"$PY" "$WORKSPACE/app/wsgi.py" >"$LOG" 2>&1 &
SERVER_PID=$!
# wait for readiness
i=0
interval=1
while [ $i -lt $MAX_WAIT ]; do
  if "$PY" - <<PYCHECK 2>/dev/null
import sys, urllib.request, json
try:
    resp=urllib.request.urlopen('http://127.0.0.1:%s/' % (%s), timeout=2)
    data=json.load(resp)
    sys.exit(0 if data.get('status')=='ok' else 4)
except Exception:
    sys.exit(3)
PYCHECK
  then
    break
  fi
  sleep $interval
  i=$((i+interval))
  if [ $interval -lt 5 ]; then interval=$((interval+1)); fi
done
# final health check
if ! "$PY" - <<PYFINAL 2>/dev/null
import sys, urllib.request, json
try:
    resp=urllib.request.urlopen('http://127.0.0.1:%s/' % (%s), timeout=3)
    data=json.load(resp)
    if data.get('status')!='ok':
        print('validation: unexpected payload', data, file=sys.stderr); sys.exit(4)
    sys.exit(0)
except Exception as e:
    print('validation: health-check failed:', e, file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(5)
PYFINAL
then
  RC=1
else
  RC=0
fi
# clean shutdown
kill -TERM "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
sleep 1
kill -KILL "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
wait "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
if [ $RC -eq 0 ]; then echo "validation: success"; exit 0; else echo "--- $LOG ---" >&2; sed -n '1,200p' "$LOG" >&2 || true; exit 6; fi
